list.title: Legal documents
list.description: The privacy policy, the terms and anything else the site has to put in writing. These are held by the CMS module and served at GET /cms/legal, which only ever answers with published documents. Note that the site's own /legal page is not wired to this yet — it still renders its own copy — so publishing here does not change what a visitor reads.
list.search_placeholder: Filter by title, slug or summary…
list.caption: Legal documents
list.empty_description: A privacy policy and a set of terms are the usual first two. Whatever you write here is what the site serves at /legal, once it is published.
list.delete_body: “{{title}}” will be removed for good, and there is no undo. A policy that was ever published is usually worth keeping as Archived instead — someone may need to know what the terms said last year.

editor.description_new: It starts as a draft — nothing reaches the public site until the status says Published.
editor.description_edit: Saving is publishing, for a document that is already published: the site reads it exactly as it stands here.
editor.document_hint: How the document is named and filed. The slug is what the public page uses in its address.
editor.text_hint: The document itself, in Markdown. This is the part visitors actually read, so it is the part worth the time.

hints.title: What the document is called, at the top of the public page.
hints.slug: Its address on the site — /legal/privacy, /legal/terms. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
hints.summary: A line or two on what this covers, for indexes and link previews. {{count}} / {{max}} characters.
hints.version: A label you choose, like 2026-08 or v3. Bumping it along with the text is what keeps a policy honest about when it changed.
hints.effective_at: When this version starts to apply. Leave it empty if it applies from the moment it is published.

status_hint.draft: Visible only in here. The public site does not serve drafts.
status_hint.published: Readable by anyone who visits the site.
status_hint.archived: Kept for the record, out of the public site.

editor.body_required: A legal document is its text — write the body before saving. The API rejects an empty one.
editor.body_placeholder:
## 1. Who we are

Write the document here…
editor.publish_body: “{{title}}” becomes publicly readable straight away: anyone visiting the site can read it, and it starts counting as what the site states. You can send it back to a draft later, but what was public was public.
editor.delete_body: “{{title}}” will be removed for good, and there is no undo. A policy that was ever published is usually worth keeping as Archived instead — someone may need to know what the terms said last year.
